paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: We introduce a new framework called Self-Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation (SELF -RAG) that enhances an LM’s quality and factuality through retrieval and self-reflection.
review_rationale: The paper introduces SELF-RAG as a retrieval-and-self-reflection framework. The body and Figure 1 describe the framework; retain as a method contribution, not as proof of universal factuality improvement.
recommended_treatment: Keep; phrase as a framework contribution.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Our framework trains a single arbitrary LM that adaptively retrieves passages on-demand, and generates and reflects on retrieved passages and its own generations using special tokens, called reflection tokens.
review_rationale: Supported: a single generator LM learns retrieval, generation, and critique using special reflection tokens and retrieved passages.
recommended_treatment: Keep; separate adaptive retrieval from reflection-token critique.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Generating reflection tokens makes the LM controllable during the inference phase, enabling it to tailor its behavior to diverse task requirements.
review_rationale: Reflection tokens enable inference-time control through configurable reward weights and retrieval thresholds. “Tailor to diverse task requirements” is a design capability, not a guarantee of successful control for every task.
recommended_treatment: Keep with capability wording and avoid guaranteed outcome language.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Experiments show that SELF RAG (7B and 13B parameters) significantly outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs and retrieval-augmented models on a diverse set of tasks.
review_rationale: The six-task superiority statement is too broad as a standalone claim. Table 2 contains task-specific exceptions, including ARC-Challenge where Self-RAG trails ChatGPT. Use the task-specific PopQA result in P019-CORR-01 and other measured comparisons instead.
recommended_treatment: Do not retain the universal superiority wording.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Specifically, SELF -RAG outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on Open-domain QA, reasoning and fact verification tasks, and it shows significant gains in improving factuality and citation accuracy for long-form generations relative to these models.1 1 I NTRODUCTION State-of-the-art LLMs continue to struggle with factual errors (Mallen et al., 2023; Min et al., 2023) despite their increased model and data scale (Ouyang et al., 2022).
review_rationale: The abstract-level comparison overstates performance across task families. Table 2 shows wins and losses depending on task and comparator; for example, Self-RAG beats retrieval-augmented ChatGPT on PopQA and PubHealth but not ARC-Challenge.
recommended_treatment: Replace with task- and comparator-specific claims.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Empirical results on six tasks, including reasoning and long-form generation, demonstrate that SELFRAG significantly outperforms pre-trained and instruction-tuned LLMs that have more parameters and widely adopted RAG approaches with higher citation accuracy.
review_rationale: This repeats the broad six-task conclusion without identifying task, metric, or baseline. Table 2 has meaningful exceptions and proprietary-model comparisons.
recommended_treatment: Do not use as an atomic empirical claim; retain only as a qualified narrative summary.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: The critic achieves a higher than 90% agreement with GPT-4-based predictions on most reflection token categories (Appendix Table 5).
manual_decision: REWRITE / QUALIFY — appendix values narrow author summary
review_rationale: The paper's prose says the critic exceeds 90% agreement with GPT-4 predictions on most categories, but the appendix's displayed Llama2-7B reward-prediction values are Retrieve 93.8%, IS_SUP 93.5%, IS_REL 80.2%, and IS_USE 73.5%. Thus only two of four displayed categories exceed 90%; preserve the exact category-level values and do not repeat 'most categories' as a verified numeric summary.
verified_source_location: PDF p. 18; Appendix reward-prediction accuracy display (Figure 5; text refers to Table 5)
recommended_treatment: Use exact category-level values; do not claim >90% for most categories or describe as human agreement.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Our approach also significantly outperforms a concurrent method that employs sophisticated prompt engineering; specifically, on the bio generation task, our 7B and 13B models outperform the concurrent CoVE (Dhuliawala et al., 2023), which iteratively prompts Llama265B to refine output.
review_rationale: Table 2 reports Bio FactScore of 81.2 (7B) and 80.2 (13B) for Self-RAG, versus 71.2 for CoVE-65B. The claim is specific to the biography-generation task and FactScore metric.
recommended_treatment: Keep with task, metric, model size and baseline named.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: On ASQA, our model shows significantly higher citation precision and recall than all models except ChatGPT.
review_rationale: ASQA citation precision is higher for Self-RAG than retrieval-augmented ChatGPT, but citation recall is lower (67.8/71.3 versus 76.6). The original wording implies superiority on both metrics and is misleading.
recommended_treatment: Replace with P019-CORR-02 exact values.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Our holistic evaluations on six tasks using multiple metrics demonstrate that SELF-RAG significantly outperforms LLMs with more parameters or with conventional retrieval-augmented generation approaches.
review_rationale: This is a repeated broad claim of holistic superiority and obscures task-level variation. It should not be treated as an atomic result.
recommended_treatment: Do not retain as an independent empirical claim.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: We therefore present Q ASPER , a dataset of 5,049 questions over 1,585 Natural Language Processing papers.
review_rationale: The paper reports 5,049 questions over 1,585 NLP papers. The body further reports an average of 3.2 questions per paper and a maximum of 12.
recommended_treatment: Keep with NLP-domain scope; canonical expanded statistic is P020-CORR-01.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: Each question is written by an NLP practitioner who read only the title and abstract of the corresponding paper, and the question seeks information present in the full text.
review_rationale: Question writers were NLP practitioners who saw only the paper title and abstract; questions target information available in the full paper.
recommended_treatment: Keep; distinguish question writers from answer annotators.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: The questions are then answered by a separate set of NLP practitioners who also provide supporting evidence to answers.
review_rationale: A separate group of NLP practitioners answered the questions and selected supporting evidence, which could include text, tables, or figures.
recommended_treatment: Keep; evidence is not limited to prose passages.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: We ﬁnd that existing models that do well on other QA tasks do not perform well on answering these questions, underperforming humans by at least 27F1 points when answering them from entire papers, motivating further research in document-grounded, information-seeking QA, which our dataset is designed to facilitate.
review_rationale: The paper reports that its best full-paper QA model trails the human lower-bound estimate by at least 27 Answer-F1 points in the reported QASPER setup. Table 2 provides exact test-set values.
recommended_treatment: Keep with benchmark split, metric and lower-bound qualification; use P020-CORR-03 for exact comparison.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: Note that given the disagreements among the workers estimated in Section 3, this is a lower bound on human performance for two reasons: ﬁrst, because only two annotations are used to compute the metric, while systems are evaluated against all three; and second, because the annotators are NLP practitioners, not expert researchers, and it is likely that an expert would score higher.
review_rationale: The authors explicitly characterize the human score as a lower bound: only two annotations are used to compute the metric while systems are evaluated against all three, and annotators are NLP practitioners rather than expert researchers.
recommended_treatment: Keep as a limitation, not a model-performance result.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: We note Lacks domain knowledge errors are not always solved by better entity type resolution (see †). results show plenty of room for improvement when compared to the estimated human performance, and suggest that QASPER could serve as a test-bed for evaluating document-grounded QA research.
review_rationale: This candidate concatenates a fragment about “Lacks domain knowledge” with unrelated prose. It is not a complete, reliably interpretable empirical claim.
recommended_treatment: Reject; do not repair by guessing intended wording.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: Materials and Methods: We developed CliVER, an end-to-end scientific Claim VERification system that leverages retrieval-augmented techni ques to automatically retrieve relevant clinical trial abstracts, extract pertinent sentences, and use the PICO framework to support or refute a scientific claim.
review_rationale: CliVER retrieves clinical-trial abstracts, extracts pertinent evidence sentences, and applies PICO framing to support/refute/neutral claim verification. This is a clinical evidence-appraisal application.
recommended_treatment: Keep as biomedical/clinical transfer evidence only, not core general-AI evidence.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: We also created an ensemble of three state-of-the-art deep learning models to classify rationale of support, refute, and neutral.
review_rationale: The abstract says “three deep learning models,” but the actual ensemble consists of two BERT-based deep models and one prompt-based T5 model. It predicts Support/Refute/Neutral labels for claim-evidence pairs; it does not “classify rationale” as phrased.
recommended_treatment: Rewrite to two deep language models plus one prompt-based model; transfer-only.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: We then constructed CoVERt, a new COVID VERification dataset comprising 15 PICO-encoded drug claims accompanied by 96 manually selected and labeled clinical trial abstracts that either support or refute each claim.
review_rationale: CoVERt contains 15 PICO-encoded COVID-19 drug claims and 96 manually selected clinical-trial abstracts. The abstracts yield 212 labeled claim-sentence pairs, including Support, Refute and Neutral; it is inaccurate to imply every abstract is only support/refute.
recommended_treatment: Keep with neutral-label clarification and clinical/COVID-19 scope.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: We used CoVERt and SciFact (a public scientific claim verifi cation dataset) to assess CliVER’s performance in predicting labels.
review_rationale: The study evaluates label prediction using SciFact development data and the newly constructed CoVERt dataset. This is a clinical-domain system evaluation.
recommended_treatment: Keep; transfer-only.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: Results: In the evaluation of label prediction accuracy on CoVERt, CliVER achieved a notable F1 score of 0.92, highlighting the efficacy of the retrieval-augmented models.
review_rationale: The 0.92 macro-average F1 is the majority-voting ensemble’s Oracle label-prediction result on CoVERt. It is not end-to-end open-setting accuracy.
recommended_treatment: Keep only with Oracle setting and CoVERt scope.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: The ensemble model outperforms each individual state-of-the-art model by an absolute increase from 3% to 11% in the F1 score.
review_rationale: The abstract’s 3%–11% improvement range is too compressed without naming settings and metrics. Main-text results report 0.93 vs 0.89 on SciFact development (+4 percentage points) and 0.92 vs 0.89 on CoVERt (+3 points) for ensemble versus best individual macro-F1.
recommended_treatment: Use exact dataset-specific macro-F1 differences; do not repeat a generalized 3%–11% statement.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: Moreover, when compared with four clinicians, CliVER achieved a precision of 79.0% for abstract retrieval, 67.4% for sentence selection, and 63.2% for label prediction, respectively.
review_rationale: The 79.0%, 67.4% and 63.2% figures are stage-specific Open-setting clinician-review measures: abstract retrieval relevance, sentence selection relevance, and label agreement. They are not three precision scores.
verified_source_location: PDF pp. 6–7; Table 4 and clinician review
recommended_treatment: Keep only with metric meaning and Open-setting denominator/context.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: Conclusion: CliVER demonstrates its early potential to automate scientific claim verification using retrieval-augmented strategies to harness the wealth of clinical trial abstracts in PubMed.
manual_decision: MOVE TO NARRATIVE — not atomic result
review_rationale: “Early potential” is an author interpretation and not a measurable empirical claim. Retain as discussion context only, not a standalone evidence row.
recommended_treatment: Do not use as a quantitative or independently verifiable finding.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: We observed that the ensemble of two deep language models and one prompt-based model improves the verification accuracy of each model by an absolute increase in the F1 score from 3% to 11% on CoVERt.
review_rationale: The ensemble improves label prediction over individual models, but the improvement should be stated with exact dataset and macro-F1 values: SciFact development 0.93 vs 0.89; CoVERt 0.92 vs 0.89.
recommended_treatment: Merge with P021-CORR-02; avoid duplicating the same finding.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: To improve verification accuracy in the clinical domain, we introduce a new Covid VERification dataset (CoVERt).
review_rationale: CoVERt is a dataset contribution for COVID-19 clinical drug-claim verification. The measurable dataset composition is more informative than the broad statement that it was introduced to improve accuracy.
recommended_treatment: Merge with P021-CORR-01; transfer-only.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: Supplementary Table S3 shows that the Majority Voting ensemble achieved the best perform­ ance with a macro-average F1 score of 0.85.
review_rationale: Supplementary Table S3 reports macro-average F1 0.85 for majority voting in the end-to-end Open sentence-selection-plus-labeling evaluation. Do not conflate this with Oracle label-only CoVERt macro-F1 0.92.
verified_source_location: PDF p. 6; Supplementary Table S3 cited in Results
recommended_treatment: Keep with Open setting and pipeline-stage scope.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: For the Neutral class, we observed a higher precision of 1.0 and a lower recall of 0.89 on CoVERt compared to those on the SciFact dataset.
review_rationale: For CoVERt, the majority-voting ensemble has Neutral precision 1.00 and recall 0.89; the corresponding SciFact development values are 0.93 and 0.95. These are class-specific Oracle label-prediction metrics.
recommended_treatment: Keep; identify CoVERt/SciFact and Oracle setting.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: We observed that the majority voting ensemble model achieved the best performance when claims were formatted using Template 2, with a macro-average F1 score of 0.93.
review_rationale: For CoVERt claim paraphrases, majority voting performs best with Template 2 at macro-average F1 0.93; Templates 1 and 3 score 0.92 and Template 4 scores 0.89.
verified_source_location: PDF p. 9; Claim variation evaluation / Supplementary Table S7
recommended_treatment: Keep; scope to the four PICO templates tested on CoVERt.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Self-RAG 7B and 13B achieve PopQA accuracy of 54.9 and 55.8, respectively, compared with 50.8 for retrieval-augmented ChatGPT and 51.8 for retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat in the reported comparison.
review_rationale: Table 2 reports PopQA accuracy 50.8 for Ret-ChatGPT, 51.8 for Ret-Llama2-chat, 54.9 for Self-RAG 7B and 55.8 for Self-RAG 13B. This is the long-tail PopQA subset under the paper’s evaluation protocol.
verified_source_location: PDF p. 8; Table 2 and evaluation setup p. 7
recommended_treatment: Keep with PopQA subset and comparator scope.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: On ASQA, Self-RAG 7B reports citation precision 66.9 and recall 67.8, while Self-RAG 13B reports precision 70.3 and recall 71.3; retrieval-augmented ChatGPT reports 65.1 and 76.6, respectively.
review_rationale: Table 2 reports ASQA citation precision/recall: Ret-ChatGPT 65.1/76.6, Self-RAG 7B 66.9/67.8, and Self-RAG 13B 70.3/71.3. Self-RAG precision is higher but recall is lower than Ret-ChatGPT.
recommended_treatment: Keep; never summarize as winning both metrics.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: The Self-RAG critic reports greater than 90% agreement with GPT-4-based predictions for most reflection-token categories; this is agreement with GPT-4 predictions, not direct human-label agreement.
manual_decision: REWRITE / QUALIFY — appendix values narrow author summary
review_rationale: The paper's prose says the critic exceeds 90% agreement with GPT-4 predictions on most categories, but the appendix's displayed Llama2-7B reward-prediction values are Retrieve 93.8%, IS_SUP 93.5%, IS_REL 80.2%, and IS_USE 73.5%. Thus only two of four displayed categories exceed 90%; preserve the exact category-level values and do not repeat 'most categories' as a verified numeric summary.
verified_source_location: PDF p. 18; Appendix reward-prediction accuracy display (Figure 5; text refers to Table 5)
recommended_treatment: Use exact category-level values; do not claim >90% for most categories or describe as human agreement.

paper_title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
original_candidate_claim: Self-RAG uses a retrieval decision token to request passages only when the model estimates that retrieval would help the continued generation, rather than always retrieving a fixed number of passages.
review_rationale: The retrieval decision token allows the model to estimate whether retrieval is useful for the next generation segment, rather than always retrieving a fixed number of passages.
recommended_treatment: Keep as a mechanism description, not evidence that retrieval decisions are always correct.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: QASPER contains 5,049 information-seeking questions over 1,585 NLP papers; each paper has an average of 3.2 questions, with up to 12 questions for one paper.
review_rationale: The dataset contains 5,049 questions across 1,585 NLP papers, averaging 3.2 questions per paper with a maximum of 12 questions for one paper.
recommended_treatment: Keep; this is the canonical expanded dataset-size claim.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: In QASPER, 55.5% of questions require evidence from multiple paragraphs, and 13% require evidence from tables or figures.
review_rationale: The paper reports that 55.5% of questions require evidence from multiple paragraphs and 13% require evidence from tables or figures.
recommended_treatment: Keep; percentages refer to QASPER annotations.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: On QASPER's test set, LED-base obtains 32.80 Answer-F1 using the full text, compared with a reported human lower bound of 60.92, a gap of 28.12 F1 points.
review_rationale: On the QASPER test set, LED-base with full text obtains Answer-F1 32.80; the reported human lower bound is 60.92, a difference of 28.12 F1 points.
recommended_treatment: Keep; human value is a lower bound, not an expert ceiling.

paper_title: A Dataset of Information-Seeking Questions and Answers Anchored in Research Papers
original_candidate_claim: On QASPER's test set, LED-base achieves Evidence-F1 29.85, while the reported human lower bound is 71.62.
review_rationale: On the QASPER test set, LED-base obtains Evidence-F1 29.85, compared with a reported human lower bound of 71.62. This is evidence selection, not answer generation.
recommended_treatment: Keep; do not conflate Evidence-F1 with Answer-F1.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: Across the test sets, Table 1 lists 315 claims in total (300 SciFact and 15 CoVERt), 379 abstracts, and 512 labeled claim-sentence pairs. The CoVERt subset itself contains 15 claims, 96 abstracts, and 212 labeled pairs: 46 Support, 60 Refute, and 106 Neutral.
review_rationale: Table 1 totals 315 claims (300 SciFact + 15 CoVERt), 379 abstracts and 512 labeled claim-sentence pairs across both test sets. CoVERt alone has 15 claims, 96 abstracts and 212 pairs: 46 Support, 60 Refute and 106 Neutral.
recommended_treatment: Keep; 315 is claim count, not pair count. P021 is transfer-only.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: In Oracle label prediction, the majority-voting ensemble reaches macro-average F1 of 0.93 on SciFact development and 0.92 on CoVERt; the best individual-model macro-average F1 is 0.89 on both datasets.
review_rationale: Majority-voting macro-average F1 is 0.93 on SciFact development and 0.92 on CoVERt; best individual-model macro-average F1 is 0.89 on each.
recommended_treatment: Keep; not end-to-end Open pipeline performance. P021 is transfer-only.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: In the Open clinician-review setting, the reported agreement/accuracy was 79.0% for abstract retrieval, 67.4% for sentence selection, and 63.2% for label prediction.
review_rationale: In the Open clinician-review setting, abstract retrieval relevance is 79.0%, sentence selection relevance is 67.4%, and label agreement is 63.2%.
recommended_treatment: Keep; do not call all three precision. P021 is transfer-only.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: The end-to-end sentence-selection-plus-labeling evaluation reports macro-average F1 of 0.85 for the majority-voting ensemble in Supplementary Table S3.
review_rationale: The Open sentence-selection-plus-labeling pipeline reports majority-voting macro-average F1 0.85 in Supplementary Table S3.
verified_source_location: PDF p. 6; Supplementary Table S3 cited in Results
recommended_treatment: Keep distinct from Oracle label-only F1. P021 is transfer-only.

paper_title: Retrieval augmented scientific claim verification
original_candidate_claim: CliVER's real-world clinician evaluation used 19 clinical research claims from six disease categories and did not measure retrieval recall because exhaustive review of all relevant PubMed abstracts was not feasible.
review_rationale: The clinician evaluation included 19 clinical research claims across six disease categories. Retrieval recall was not measured because exhaustive review of all relevant PubMed abstracts was infeasible.
recommended_treatment: Keep as a limitation; P021 is transfer-only.
